method.label: Find the center using perpendicular lines

annotationRationale: Equal tangent lengths place the tangent intersection on the perpendicular bisector. Perpendicular radius slopes and intersecting line equations determine the center, and coordinate distance gives the radius squared.
sourceMethod: Followed the official coordinate alternative, expanding the calculation of the center and using radius squared directly to compute the area.

review.mathCheck: The perpendicular bisector is \(y=3x-15\), giving \(T=(5,0)\). Radius perpendicularity gives \(x+13y=175\), hence \(O=(37/4,51/4)\). Both endpoint distances squared equal \(170/16=85/8\), so the area is \(85\pi/8\), choice C. The construction is unique and consistent with the supplied source figure.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA AMC 10B solution 23's second approach, pages 11 and 12. It explains the perpendicular-bisector justification and expands the same center-coordinate calculation into reconstructible steps.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed/support split is appropriate. Unlisted point-slope form (cnm_h169) and circle area (cnm_p192) are routine background at this level, with no material instructional omission.
